findings.text: blocking: the landing fragment's comparison paragraph states the first-round Jev arm's result as 'three members stamped with after-scores 0.875/0.91875/0.89375'. Those are the first round's BEFORE scores, not its after-scores: the parent revision's record at docs/evidence/fragments/sn-selection-over-generation/ssog-anchor-ab/vertical_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture-jev.json records scores_before {vertical 0.875, x 0.91875, y 0.89375} and scores_after {vertical 1.0, x 1.0, y 0.875} (git show 284f17bcba6f17457c54d40527d5f1776f6fa0e9:<path>). The re-run's own scores_before are the same three numbers, which is where the sentence's figures appear to come from. The paragraph therefore misstates the baseline it compares against and overstates the re-run's improvement: against the true first-round after-scores the only documentation move the re-run makes is the anchor member, y_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture 0.875 to 1.0, where the fragment reads as though all three members rose. The fragments are the evidence the coordinator's adoption call reads, so a wrong baseline belongs to the deliverable rather than to a summary of it.

follow-on: nothing asserts the receipt's required field set, so the change has no guard that fails if it regresses. The done_when names outcome_status, anchor, lint before and after, per-member documentation scores before and after, batches run, calls, spend, wall time, stamped, containment and the code digest; this node adds no test, and no test in tests/ reads this record (grep over tests/ for outcome_status/ssog-anchor-ab finds only unrelated matches in tests/standard_names/test_export_tombstone_selection.py and tests/standard_names/test_rerank_label_sheet.py). The one consumer, docs/evidence/fragments/sn-selection-over-generation/ssog-anchor-ab-aggregate-run.py:261 with :137-139, degrades rather than failing: _classify substitutes {} for a missing scores_after and _family_verdict then reports the arm as 'no completed record', so a receipt that lost scores_after, batches_run or lint_after would be read as an absent arm instead of an error. Testing this fragment family is an established idiom (tests/standard_names/test_rerank_label_sheet.py loads an ssog runner script directly), so a schema assertion on the receipt is available rather than novel.
